prompts.title: AGENTS.md starter
prompts.description: Rules file that Claude Code and Codex read at the start of every session

prompts.title: Meeting notes to action items
prompts.description: Fill-in template that turns rough notes into owners and dates
prompts.body:
Turn these meeting notes into a short summary and a list of action items.

Notes:
{{notes}}

People in the meeting: {{people:everyone mentioned in the notes}}

Format:
**Decided**: one line per decision.
**Actions**: one line each, as "Owner: task, by date". If no date was said, write "date not set".
**Open questions**: anything left unanswered.

Don't add anything that isn't in the notes.

prompts.title: Review this diff like a senior engineer
prompts.description: A focused code review that ranks problems by how much they matter
prompts.body:
Review the diff below as a senior {{language:TypeScript}} engineer.

Focus on {{focus:correctness, edge cases and security}}. For each problem:
1. Quote the line.
2. Say what goes wrong and when.
3. Suggest the smallest fix.

Rank problems from most to least serious. Skip style nits unless they hide a bug.
End with one sentence: is this safe to merge as is?

{{diff}}

prompts.title: Turn a bug report into a fix plan
prompts.description: Agent brief that reproduces a bug first, then fixes it with a test
prompts.body:
Here is a bug report:

{{bug}}

Before changing any code:
1. Find where this happens. Start in {{area:the part of the code the report mentions}}.
2. Write a failing test that shows the bug.
3. Explain the cause in two or three sentences.

Then fix it with the smallest change that makes the test pass, run the full test suite, and tell me what you changed and why.

prompts.title: Write plainly
prompts.description: System prompt for short, clear answers without filler
prompts.body:
Write the way a sharp colleague talks.

- Lead with the answer, then the reason.
- Short sentences. Common words. No filler like "Great question".
- Use lists only when the order or the count matters.
- If you're unsure, say so and say what would settle it.
- Never invent facts, names, numbers or links.

skills.name: commit-message
skills.description: Writes a clear git commit message for the staged changes. Use when the user asks to commit, wants a commit message, or says "write the commit".

skills.name: release-notes
skills.description: Writes user-facing release notes from merged commits, pull requests or a changelog. Use when preparing a release, bumping a version, or writing a "what's new" post.
